page: Microsoft Azure F48alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Faldsv7 family, powered by a dedicated 48-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, this server features a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, providing 96.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). It includes a substantial local storage allocation of 5669 GB NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage. The processor features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and cryptographic accelerators like AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48alds_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as PassMark CPU and physics tests. Its memory subsystem delivers strong throughput, with read-only small block cached bandwidth in the top 10% and large block read/write speeds in the top 25%. Storage and database performance are also highly competitive, with Redis SET operations and PassMark database operations ranking in the top 10%.

For specialized workloads, the server excels at compression and decompression tasks, scoring in the top 10% for single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3. Large language model inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing for small models and text generation for medium models, though performance drops to average levels for large 70B models due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration.

Given its high-frequency dedicated cores, low memory density, and massive local NVMe storage, the F48alds_v7 offers high cost efficiency for compute-heavy and IOPS-intensive workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is highly suited for high-performance computing, web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
